in.other_title: Majority voting performs on par with multi-agent debate across benchmarks
in.rationale: Du et al. report multi-agent debate beats majority vote on arithmetic (81.8% vs 69.0%) and GSM8K (85.0% vs 81.0%) with 3 ChatGPT agents and 2 rounds. Choi, Zhu and Li report majority voting performs on par with MAD in most cases on benchmarks including Arithmetics and GSM8K with 5 Qwen2.5 or Llama3.1 agents, concluding MAD's gains come mostly from ensembling.
in.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether multi-agent debate beats majority voting over the same agents on arithmetic and GSM8K

open_obligations: Check that the 'prior strategy from [2]' in Table 9 matches the answer-extraction code actually used by Du et al.
Check whether Du et al.'s majority-vote baseline is comparable to the authors' T = 0 majority voting over 5 agents
Confirm the critique is shown only on GSM8K with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and not on Du et al.'s ChatGPT setting
in.other_title: Choi et al. argue Du et al.'s reported MAD gains over majority voting partly reflect answer parsing
in.rationale: Du et al. report that multiagent debate beats single-agent, reflection and majority-vote baselines on arithmetic and GSM8K; the authors argue this evaluation is confounded by answer parsing. They back the argument with one GSM8K comparison (Table 9, p25 L211-216, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) where single-agent accuracy under their extraction exceeds MAD scored with Du et al.'s strategy, so this is a methodological critique rather than a rerun of Du et al.'s ChatGPT experiments.
in.scope: proposed CRITIQUES: Whether MAD's reported advantage over majority voting and single agents survives a standardized final-answer extraction protocol
